documents.title_en: NOTICE TO ALL TENANTS: Underground Parking Garage Repaving

blocks.text_en:
Please be advised that Crestview Tower Management will resurface and repaint both levels of the underground parking garage next week. To minimize disruption to commuters, the work will be completed in two phases:

• Phase 1 (Level B1): Closed from Monday, November 9, at 6:00 A.M. through Tuesday, November 10, at 8:00 P.M.
• Phase 2 (Level B2): Closed from Wednesday, November 11, at 6:00 A.M. through Thursday, November 12, at 8:00 P.M.

During each closure, monthly pass holders who normally park on the affected level may use the overflow surface lot on Elm Street at no extra cost by displaying their yellow hangtag on the rearview mirror. Please note that the electric vehicle charging stations on Level B1 will be shut off during Phase 1; drivers requiring charging stations on Monday or Tuesday should use the public charging hub across from City Hall.

blocks.text_en:
To: Kenneth Cho <k.cho@bistrocollective.com>
From: Nadia Al-Mansoor <nalmansoor@kilncraftceramics.com>
Date: October 19
Subject: Thermal Shock Test Results — Verona Stoneware Line

Dear Mr. Cho,

Thank you for visiting our showroom last week to evaluate tableware options for Bistro Collective's upcoming restaurant openings in Denver and Salt Lake City. During our meeting, you asked whether the matte glaze on our Verona Stoneware soup bowls could withstand high-temperature commercial dishwashers without chipping or fading.

Our quality assurance lab completed a 200-cycle thermal durability test yesterday, and I am pleased to report that all twelve test bowls showed zero surface wear or discoloration. I have attached the official laboratory certificate to this message for your review.

In addition, I have dispatched a box containing four sample place settings in the olive-green finish to your Denver regional office via express courier. Once your culinary team has had a chance to inspect the samples, please let me know how many sets you would like to include in your initial purchase order so we can reserve kiln capacity for November.

Best regards,
Nadia Al-Mansoor
Commercial Accounts Manager, KilnCraft Ceramics

documents.title_en: Portland's Commercial Green-Roof Rebate Draws Strong Corporate Interest

blocks.text_en:
PORTLAND (October 22) — Since the Portland Office of Sustainability launched its Commercial Rooftop Canopy Grant eighteen months ago, thirty-four office and warehouse properties across the metropolitan area have converted bare tar rooftops into vegetated gardens. [[position:1]] Under the municipal initiative, commercial building owners receive a rebate of $15 per square meter—up to a maximum of $45,000 per property—to offset the cost of waterproof membranes, lightweight soil, and drought-tolerant native plants.

City engineers designed the program primarily to reduce stormwater runoff into the Willamette River during heavy autumn rains. [[position:2]] However, participating businesses report that the thermal insulation provided by the soil layer has delivered an equally valuable financial benefit. At Cascade Logistics Center, a 4,000-square-meter distribution warehouse near the port, summer air-conditioning expenses dropped by 22 percent during the first year after installation. [[position:3]]

Because the initial grant fund has been nearly exhausted, the City Council voted last week to allocate an additional $1.8 million for the upcoming fiscal year. [[position:4]] Applications for the next funding round open on January 15, and priority will be given to industrial buildings with flat roofs exceeding 1,500 square meters.

choices.text_en: To attract landscaping companies to relocate to Portland
To decrease the amount of rainwater flowing into a local river

To replace solar panels on older industrial warehouses

To: Priya Nair <pnair@oceanicunderwriting.com>

I am writing with a scheduling request regarding your presentation at the Pacific Rim Supply Chain Forum this Friday, November 14. Dr. Henrik Lindholm's incoming flight from Stockholm was rescheduled by the airline, and he will now land in Vancouver at 1:30 P.M. on Friday. Consequently, he will not be able to reach the convention center in time for his 1:00 P.M. slot.

Please let me know by 5:00 P.M. today whether this arrangement works for you, and remember to upload your final slide deck to the speaker portal by Wednesday.

Sincerely,
Gavin Cho

documents.title_en: Bellini Commercial Espresso Systems — Limited Warranty Policy

blocks.text_en:
1. Coverage Period: Bellini Commercial Espresso Systems warrants the Dual-Boiler Pro 3000 against defects in internal mechanical and electrical components—including the brass brew group, rotary water pump, and digital pressure control board—for twenty-four (24) months from the original date of purchase.

2. Exclusions: This limited warranty does not cover rubber portafilter gaskets, external milk carafes, or damage caused by failure to use a certified water-softening filter. Replacement of excluded accessories is billed at standard catalog rates.

3. On-Site Service & Shipping: During the first twelve (12) months of ownership, Bellini provides complimentary on-site technician dispatch within 80 kilometers of an authorized service center. In months 13 through 24, replacement covered parts remain free of charge, but a flat $85 technician travel fee applies to all on-site visits.

Issue Description: Yesterday morning, the digital pressure control board stopped displaying the boiler temperature, and the right-hand steam wand began losing pressure. We have always used the official Bellini water-softening filter cartridge and replaced it every ninety days as instructed. In addition to repairing the pressure control board, please have the technician bring two new rubber portafilter gaskets, as ours are worn.
